title: Clogged Dryer Vent in Statesboro GA | Causes & Solutions
description: Learn the common causes and warning signs of a clogged dryer vent in Statesboro, including lint buildup, crushed ducts, bird nests, long runs, and blocked exterior vents.
h1: What to Do About a Clogged Dryer Vent
intro: A clogged dryer vent means the exhaust path is restricted enough to interfere with normal airflow. Lint is a common cause, but it is not the only one. A useful diagnosis looks at the entire route from the dryer connection to the exterior termination.

sections.body: Lint buildup, crushed transition ducts, long vent runs, multiple elbows, nesting material, stuck exterior flaps, and disconnected or damaged duct sections can all interfere with airflow.

sections.h2: Symptoms that can point to the vent
sections.body: Longer cycles, unusually hot laundry, weak airflow outside, excess lint, or a dryer that repeatedly stops can be consistent with a restricted vent. None of those symptoms should be treated as proof by themselves.

Homeowners can inspect the lint screen, look for an obviously crushed connection behind the dryer, and observe whether air is leaving the exterior termination while the dryer runs. Hidden ducts, roof exits, electrical issues, and disassembly are different matters.
If lint is the problem, cleaning may restore airflow. If the vent is crushed, separated, or improperly routed, the solution may require repair or replacement instead.

faqs.q: Can I tell if a dryer vent is clogged from outside?
faqs.a: Sometimes. Weak airflow or a flap that barely opens can be clues, but the location and cause of a restriction may still be hidden inside the duct.

faqs.q: Can a new dryer still have vent problems?
faqs.a: Yes. The vent belongs to the building rather than the appliance, so replacing the dryer does not automatically correct an existing exhaust restriction.
